rv.q: Superbly directed by Diane Paulus, with a stellar octet of players headed by John Turturro and Paul Giamatti

The A.R.T. has tinkered with the long-standard English translation by Derek Prouse, cutting some minor characters and streamlining scenes, but they’ve thankfully resisted the temptation to overplay any correlations to current movements or people — no orange wigs or red hats on the rhinos — in part because they don’t have to.
Fortunately, the actors were usually able to bring the energy back with a sharp joke, quick exchange, or burst of physical comedy.

cn.t: Critics praise this darkly funny, chillingly prescient revival of Ionesco's absurdist classic, with Turturro and Giamatti leading a stunning cast through a timely examination of conformity that's hilarious in the first half, bone-chilling in the second.
